text:
maya: Quick sync — thinking about a "QoS bundle" add-on for pricing: priority routing, per-request SLAs, burst guarantees. Thoughts? :thinking:

devon: Two customers asked for this in demos last week. they'd pay for priority if it's predictable.

sam: Need to model margin. If we give network priority, cost could rise >40% on peak. show me numbers before we commit.

liam: Legal: we can offer SLA but need clear exceptions + force majeure + credit calc. Don’t want open-ended obligations.

nina: From infra POV: implementing strict QoS across hosted + dedicated + private is painful. Need toggles per-tenant + telemetry.

maya: Agree. Proposal: bundle includes "priority route" + 99.9% tail p95 <= 120ms for text-gen. Pilot for Dedicated customers only.

jordan: Launch criteria suggestion: 1) Pricing SKU defined 2) 1 pilot customer COMMITTED 3) SLO runbook + fallbacks in console 4) cost model validated.

nina: For fallbacks we should auto-route to 'best-effort' model variant. That requires KV cache affinity and routing policy changes.

ops-bot: runbook link: https://internal.redwood/runbooks/qos-bundle (permissions required)

devon: Sales motion: propose list price + discount tiers. Will test demand w/ 3 leads. Any rough $/month idea?

sam: Ballpark: premium ~20-30% uplift on unit price OR fixed monthly seat for guaranteed capacity. Need elasticity sim.

ollie: From platform strategy: prefer per-token uplift to avoid seat locking. But customers in enterprise like committed guarantees.

liam: Contract exceptions: cap credits to avoid runaway liability. e.g., credits = min(30 days fees, 3x monthly) — draft language incoming.

maya: Can we scope to Dedicated first, then expand to Hosted after 2 quarters? That reduces initial infra risk.

nina: Yes — Dedicated has existing isolation. Hosted needs routing tier in front of model pool.

jordan: Action items: maya to draft SKU + launch checklist, sam to run margin sim, liam to draft SLA language, devon to line up pilots. Timeline: 3 weeks?

maya: I’ll draft and post a PR to roadmaps. Thanks all. :raised_hands:
